item.title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
item.description: arXiv:2610.30192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Nima Moshayedi

item.title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
item.description: arXiv:2610.30304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.
item.dc:creator: L. Cherepanov, S. Khoroshkin

item.title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.30317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.
item.dc:creator: L. Cherepanov

item.title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
item.description: arXiv:2610.30542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.
item.dc:creator: E. Notte-Cuello, J. M. Hoff da Silva

item.title: First-order differential constraints for the nonlinear wave equation:wave fronts, admissible nonlinearities and exact solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct exact solutions of the nonlinear wave equation in three space dimensions by the method of linear determining equations: first-order constraint functions are found as solutions of the linear determining equation, the differential constraints obtained by setting them equal to zero are integrated, and the resulting ansatz is substituted into the equation. Lie point symmetries are a special case, and the solutions obtained generically have no symmetry. The determining equations tie the admissible nonlinearity to the geometry of the constraint: arbitrary on characteristic hyperplanes, cubic on light cones, and, for a pair of constraints, exponential on light cones and quintic on the cylindrical fronts of a line source. Among the solutions are smooth bounded sine-Gordon walls and vortex configurations whose shape varies arbitrarily along a front, the fields of point sources moving on arbitrary trajectories for the cubic and Liouville equations, with an exact nonlinear analogue of the Larmor formula for the power radiated in the cubic case, and smooth finite-energy solutions of the cubic equation with any prescribed number of toroidal nodal surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Kaptsov

item.title: A sharp gradient-corrected Lieb--Thirring inequality in one dimension with applications to density functional theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.30887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We first prove a sharp Lieb-Thirring inequality with semi-classical constant and gradient correction in one dimension. In the periodic setting, the corresponding inequality also includes a parity dependent shell-correction term, which appears to be new. Moreover, we also characterize the optimizers of these inequalities. In particular, the optimizing density profiles form a two-dimensional manifold, which we call here the Poincar\'e density manifold. We then apply these results to study the Thomas--Fermi--von Weizs\"acker (TFW) approximation of the kinetic energy in Density Functional Theory. More precisely, we first obtain an explicit and non-asymptotic bound on the global and local error made by the TFW approximation. These bounds are controlled by the distance of the normalized density profile from the Poincar\'e density manifold times the number of particles. In particular, these bounds show that the TFW approximation is exact on the Poincar\'e manifold. We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincar\'e manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit $N \rightarrow \infty$ with asymptotic rate of order $N^{-2}$. This rate is shown to be optimal.
item.dc:creator: Thiago Carvalho Corso, Louis Garrigue

item.title: Dirac Structures and Reduction of Optimal Control Problems with Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.31033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the symmetry reduction of optimal control problems using Dirac structures. The first-order conditions of the Pontryagin Maximum Principle are written as an implicit Dirac system on the Pontryagin bundle. For a problem invariant under a Lie group, we reduce both the Lagrange-Pontryagin variational principle and the underlying Dirac structure, and prove that they yield the same reduced equations, which we identify with the Hamiltonian equations on the dual of the Atiyah algebroid. Reconstruction, independence of the principal connection, and the relation between criticality and optimality complete the picture. Dropping regularity, we give the Gotay-Nester-Hinds constraint algorithm a Dirac-geometric form and prove that symmetry reduction commutes with it. For control-linear systems whose admissible directions are horizontal for a principal connection, abnormal extremals lie on the leaf where the base costate vanishes, and the first secondary constraint is the degeneracy of the curvature pairing. We also give a reduced criterion for strict abnormality and a metric-free index form. Examples: a spacecraft with rotors (flat connection), the Heisenberg group (nowhere-zero curvature) and the Martinet problem (curvature vanishing on a hypersurface).
item.dc:creator: A. Ibort, M. Leok, R. Salmoni, C. Sard\'on

item.title: Hadamard states for linearized gravity on asymptotically flat spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the quantization of linearized Einstein equations on 4-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. We prove the existence of fully gauge invariant Hadamard states in the harmonic gauge for any Einstein metric asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity.
item.dc:creator: Christian G\'erard, Mikhail Molodyk, Micha{\l} Wrochna

item.title: Symmetric and antisymmetric cumulant hierarchies and Wick polynomials of operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.31374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There has been much progress in understanding mathematical foundations of kinetic theory in recent years, in particular, for the original model of a rarefied gas of classical particles with repulsive interactions, as well as for weakly nonlinear wave evolutions related to wave turbulence. These results are mainly based on refined analysis of evolution hierarchies of moments of the relevant random variables, or of related quantities such as of cumulants or of correlation errors. In this work, we extend two of such basic tools, cumulants and Wick polynomials, to a setting where the random variables no longer need to commute, with the goal of handling expectations of creation and annihilation operators on a Fock space, both in the bosonic and fermionic case. We call these constructions symmetric and antisymmetric cumulants and Wick polynomials, respectively. As an application, we derive a hierarchy of evolution equations satisfied by such cumulants, usually called truncated correlation functions in this context, for a gas of bosons or fermions hopping on a finite lattice and interacting via a two-body potential. With sufficient control over solutions to these hierarchies, one could control the magnitude of the error terms related to an approximation of the state of the quantum system by a finite lattice kinetic equation studied in our earlier work, closely connected to standard bosonic and fermionic Boltzmann--Nordheim equations.
item.dc:creator: Jani Lukkarinen, Sakari Pirnes

item.title: An elliptic generalization of the $D^{(2)}_{2}$ Spin chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.31381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An integrable elliptic generalization of the closed $D^{(2)}_2$ quantum spin chain is constructed. Taking the trigonometric limit, we have shown that the corresponding R-matrix reduces to that of the $D^{(2)}_2$ one, up to a similarity transformation. Basing on the very fact of the factorization for the R-matrix and the corresponding transfer matrix which indeed ensures the integrability of the model, we give the exact solution of the model which can be expressed in terms of a homogeneous T-Q relation.
item.dc:creator: Yi Qiao, Pei Sun, Xiaotian Xu, Junpeng Cao, Guang-Liang Li, Wen-Li Yang, Kangjie Shi, Yupeng Wang

item.title: Some minimal characteristics and flat trajectories of a system in the N-body problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.31582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the classical model of a system of N particles with interaction (the N-body problem) we consider some spatial problems of nonlinear programming for finding conditional minima and local extrema for the main characteristics of the system on its phase space. We prove that these conditional minima and local extrema of the system characteristics can only be achieved on flat, in general, not necessarily finite, trajectories of the system in space, (under the condition that the system angular momentum is non-zero). And then we find the basic conditions limiting the values of the integrals of motion: angular momentum and total energy of the system under which these trajectories are flat finite ("circular" or elliptical) trajectories on which the flat structure of the system is preserved in time under the certain restrictions on the values of the system's integrals of motion. And we determine also the values of the system's key characteristics on these flat trajectories. Next, in the Appendix, we consider some additional related results for a more general model of the system.
item.dc:creator: Igor Pavlov

item.title: Mutual transformations of arbitrary ternary qubit trees by Clifford gates
item.description: arXiv:2404.16693v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is shown that ternary qubit trees with the same number of nodes can be transformed by the naturally defined sequence of Clifford gates into each other or into standard representation as one-dimensional chain corresponding to Jordan-Wigner transform.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Yu. Vlasov

item.title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
item.description: arXiv:2610.30242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.
item.dc:creator: Federico Ambrosino, Anatoly Konechny, Ingo Runkel, G\'erard M. T. Watts

item.title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.30247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Jeevan Chandra, Diego Liska, Boris Post

item.title: Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
item.description: arXiv:2610.30331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.
item.dc:creator: Jack Luong, Reed Spitzer, Scott D. Ramsey, Andrea L. Bertozzi, Roy Baty

item.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.30395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.
item.dc:creator: Ruben Louis

item.title: Normal Matrix Model and Hyperelliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.30475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a two-matrix model with a normal matrix with eigenvalues confined to contours in the upper half plane coupled to a Hermitian matrix. This generalizes the matrix model proposed by Jens Hoppe which corresponds to a single horizontal line. We solve the saddle point equations for several lines and show that the large-N free energy can be expressed in terms of hyperelliptic integrals. We show that the model describes a Coulomb gas in the presence of an infinite conducting boundary.
item.dc:creator: Valdemar Melin

item.title: Entropy bounded compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for hyperbolic conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2610.30496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.
item.dc:creator: Deepak Kumar, Pratima Rai, Arvind Patel

item.title: When Language Models Misinterpret Uncertainty in Earth System Mechanism Attribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.30501v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mechanistic attribution in Earth system science requires quantifying uncertainty and communicating its implications. Here, we develop an uncertainty-aware mechanistic attribution pipeline that constructs probabilistic fingerprints from ensemble estimates, including covariance-aware separation of competing mechanisms, and an evidence ladder that systematically varies the information provided to language models (LLMs). We evaluate this framework in an idealized stochastic system and a coupled El Ni\~no model using controlled interventions and ensemble data assimilation. In the idealized system, numerical separation increases GPT-4o's intervention-label agreement from 0.80 to 0.98, but not GPT-4o-mini's. In the coupled system, both LLMs identify seven of eight fingerprint-ambiguous events when given full fingerprints with verbal interpretations; GPT-4o's false ambiguity reports decrease from 10/82 to 1/82, without consistent gains in intervention-label agreement. For eight historical ENSO events, the uncertainty-aware condition agrees with the model-inferred mechanism labels in seven cases. These findings distinguish uncertainty assessment from its communication.
item.dc:creator: Pouria Behnoudfar, Nan Chen

item.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, II: local perturbations, the scattering matrix and an inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.30575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Robin, or impedance, Laplacian on a half-space of dimension $n \ge 3$ which is perturbed inside a fixed ball. The boundary may be deformed, and obstacles may be present in the interior or attached to the boundary, in any combination and with no smallness assumption. Outside the ball the configuration is the flat impedance half-space of Part I, with constant impedance $\alpha > 0$, where a bulk channel and a surface channel propagate at every positive energy and only the surface channel propagates on the band $(-\alpha^2,0)$. We prove a limiting absorption principle, valid at every positive energy and outside a discrete set of embedded eigenvalues in the band. We construct the generalized Fourier transform and prove its completeness by a stationary argument which constructs no wave operator and reduces completeness to the uniqueness of the scattering solution at each energy. We then obtain the scattering matrix, its unitarity and a two-channel optical theorem. The main result is a uniqueness theorem for the inverse problem. Under two geometric conditions on the pair, the scattering amplitude at a single positive energy determines the perturbation completely, and the argument does not distinguish a deformation of the boundary from an obstacle. It follows that no nontrivial perturbation satisfying the same conditions is invisible at any positive energy. On the surface band the corresponding statement is reduced to one explicitly stated question about the exterior Robin problem.
item.dc:creator: Michiyuki Watanabe

item.title: Hasegawa-Mima equation as limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system
item.description: arXiv:2610.30788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the Hasegawa-Mima equation (HME) is the limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system in a special scaling regime. The proof relies on the derivation of a uniform estimate independent of the scaling parameter, using the particular structure of the singular system and the identification of a combination of the unknowns that compensates for fast oscillations in time. We also show that HME allow us to investigate a conditional property of inverse energy cascade and drift waves.
item.dc:creator: Federico Butori, Franco Flandoli, Yassine Tahraoui

item.title: Surface Defects in the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Lens Space Index and Elliptic Integrability
item.description: arXiv:2610.30849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the surface-defect difference operators of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ lens space index for class $\mathcal{S}$ theories of type $A_{N-1}$ on $(\mathbb{S}^3/\mathbb{Z}_r)\times\mathbb{S}^1$. For generic fugacities $(p,q,t)$ and arbitrary rank $N$, orbifold order $r$ and discrete holonomies, their coefficients are finite products of theta functions with nomes $p^r$ and $q^r$. After an explicit gauge transformation, Gaussian in the holonomies, each operator factorizes into two elliptic Ruijsenaars--Schneider-type operators with step $pq$, one with nome $p^r$ and one with nome $q^r$, acting on variables glued along a lattice. Using this factorization and a Wronski-type relation, we prove that all the operators commute. We also establish a sufficient criterion for self-adjointness with respect to the bilinear vector multiplet pairing. It applies to the basic mixed operator and, in suitable parameter chambers, to the pure $p$- and $q$-type operators; for general mixed operators the contour prescription remains open. These results support the expectations from S-duality.
item.dc:creator: Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: Stiff source terms inside ADER-DG method
item.description: arXiv:2610.30852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: ADER-DG numerical method with the LST-DG predictor, when used to solve hyperbolic equations with stiff source terms, exhibits properties characteristic of IMEX computational schemes. With increasing stiffness, characterized by the parameter $z = \nu{\Delta t}^{n} < 0$, the maximum of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}$ of the ADER-DG numerical method increases. In the region of strong stiffness $|z| \gg 1$, a linear increase in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z) \sim |z|$ occurs. In the region of small source terms $|z| \ll 1$, the results $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ transform into known results for the problem $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(0)$ without source terms. In the transition region $|z| \sim 1$, a range of insignificant decrease in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ is discovered. In the linear case, instability is violated precisely when one of the matrix eigenvalues reaches $\lambda = -1$, regardless of the phase $\theta$ of the numerical solution. A rigorous stability theory of the ADER-DG numerical method for stiff problems for arbitrary degree $N$ of basis polynomials is constructed. The stability condition is simplified to solving a polynomial equation for the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}$. Highly accurate dependencies of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(N, z)$ of the ADER-DG method on the parameter $z$ are obtained. A rigorous direct proof of the approximation of the ADER-DG method is presented. Approximation orders $p = N+1$ for arbitrary degrees $N$ are rigorously derived. A set of numerical experiments is carried out to apply the ADER-DG method to solving both a linear advection-reaction equation and the system of Euler equations for a two-component reacting medium. The results obtained in these calculations confirm the theoretical results well.
item.dc:creator: I. S. Popov, A. P. Popova

item.title: Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string-amplitude building blocks from the intersection matrix
item.description: arXiv:2610.30862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.
item.dc:creator: Yi-xiao Tao, Shijie Zhang

item.title: Initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations on the half-line. We first give a systematic account of fundamental solutions for equations with general finite-range interactions. We then develop complementary approaches based on reflection, the Laplace transform, and the unified transform method, obtaining contour integral and Bessel-function representations of solutions. For the semidiscrete diffusion equation, we justify these representations for continuous boundary data and initial data of polynomial growth, establish uniqueness in the corresponding growth class, and derive spatial estimates and long-time properties, including asymptotic periodicity. We also treat nonhomogeneous equations, Robin boundary conditions, nonsymmetric coefficients, and a class of time-dependent coefficients. Finally, higher-order examples illustrate how the unified transform approach extends beyond second-order equations.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Chatziafratis, Spyridon Kamvissis, Anton\'in Slav\'ik

item.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.31191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.
item.dc:creator: Mich\`ele Levi

item.title: Chaos of Caputo derivative
item.description: arXiv:2610.31255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fr\'echet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.
item.dc:creator: El-Mahdi Nafia, Aziz El Ghazouani, M'hamed El Omari

item.title: Exact stress-tensor generators distinguish integrable continuations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The same leading $T\bar T$ interaction can coexist with sharply different strong-field responses, even within causal, classically integrable sigma models. We reconstruct exact autonomous stress-tensor generators for prescribed one-scale Courant--Hilbert families in two dimensions. Separating the invariant stress scale from a signed trace ratio reduces reconstruction to one scalar inversion on each invertible physical branch. The resulting profile determines both the deformation law and the relation between local energy density and pressure. For generalized Born--Infeld and logarithmic models, the leading interactions coincide, yet pressure saturates in the former and grows without bound in the latter. Their exact generators are respectively quadratic and nonpolynomial, the latter involving Lambert $W_{-1}$. A regular Legendre transformation gives the same profile in the auxiliary potential formulation. The flows commute locally with root-$T\bar T$ within a common smooth branch and retain a common classical Lax form. Exact reconstruction thus quantifies the nonlinear freedom left by leading-order matching.
item.dc:creator: H. Babaei-Aghbolagh, Song He, Zahra Pezhman

item.title: Atomic limits of empirical measures of interacting particle systems with self-duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.31319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the fixed-particle limit of empirical measures for a unified self-dual family of conservative particle systems on $\mathbb{Z}^d$: independent random walkers, the symmetric exclusion process, and the symmetric inclusion process. For a fixed number of particles $k$, under diffusive space-time scaling parametrised by $n$, we prove that as $n\to\infty$ the normalised empirical measure converges in $D([0,T],\mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ to an atomic empirical measure carried by $k$ independent diffusions, with constant covariance determined by the microscopic jump kernel. Equivalently, the limit is the unique atomic solution of the Dean-Kawasaki martingale problem with mass quantisation $1/k$. In particular, exclusion and inclusion have the same fixed-$k$ atomic limit as independent walkers: the interaction contributes only through microscopic near-collisions, whose rescaled occupation time vanishes. The proof combines self-duality, consistency-based reduction to two particles, and Green-function estimates for finite perturbations of symmetric random walks.
item.dc:creator: Mario Ayala, Nicolas Dirr, Johannes Zimmer

item.title: Explicit quasi-periodic solutions to the discrete derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quasi-periodic solutions to the discrete derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation are investigated. A Lax pair of the discrete integrable equation is derived, by which we obtain a nonlinear integrable symplectic map. Resorting to this map, the Riemann theta function expressions for discrete potentials are calculated. Consequently, we get the explicit solutions for the discrete derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, whose quasi-periodic properties are illustrated through the cases of genus one and genus two.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxue Xu, Wei Liu, Junyi Zhu

item.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions I: Algebra, geometry, and a spin model
item.description: arXiv:2610.31485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a family of five-dimensional non-flexible quadratic real algebras $\{\mathcal A_\gamma\}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}$ with canonical basis $1,i,j,k,\ell$, in which $\gamma$ changes the multiplication but not their norm, and study how this change affects geometry and dynamics. The algebras are pairwise non-isomorphic, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra, and $\mathcal A_1$ is the Pentarnion algebra. The alternating part of the trilinear form $\langle u\times_\gamma v,w\rangle$ induced by the multiplication of $\mathcal{A}_\gamma$ defines a three-dimensional subspace $H_\gamma\subset\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k,\ell\}$, tilted by the angle $\arctan(\gamma/\sqrt3)$, whose rotation group $G_\gamma\cong\mathrm{SO}(3)$ contains the automorphism group of $\mathcal A_\gamma$. For $\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2$ the groups $G_{\gamma_1}$ and $G_{\gamma_2}$ generate $\mathrm{SO}(V)\cong\mathrm{SO}(4)$. For the six ways of ordering and bracketing the product of $i,p,p$ in $\mathcal A_\gamma$, two map the unit circle in ${\rm span}\{j,k\}$ to a point and, for $\gamma>0$, four map it to ellipses. As an application, we derive a Hamiltonian model of a classical spin on $H_\gamma$ whose multiplication-induced quadratic energy is isotropic for $\gamma=0$ and anisotropic for $\gamma>0$. It conserves spin length and, for fixed $\gamma$, energy, and satisfies an exact work identity when $\gamma$ varies in time. Numerical experiments with periodically varying $\gamma$ indicate both regular and irregular spin dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Poshtkohi, Susanne Pumpluen

item.title: Sign-problem-free Bosonic Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2610.31541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The sign problem poses a fundamental barrier to numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, severely hindering our understanding of quantum many-body physics across disciplines ranging from condensed matter to particle and nuclear physics. Geometrical frustration makes this barrier especially acute for interacting bosons. Here, we develop a bosonic auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (BAFQMC) method and rigorously prove that time-reversal symmetry and reflection positivity each provide a general sufficient condition for sign-problem-free simulations. Crucially, under either criterion, BAFQMC evades the sign problem even on frustrated lattices where conventional world-line and stochastic-series-expansion methods fail. Benchmarking our approach on a two-flavor Bose-Hubbard model on the triangular lattice yields excellent quantitative agreement with finite-temperature exact diagonalization. By establishing unifying principles to solve the sign problem in BAFQMC, our work substantially expands the reach of unbiased, numerically exact simulations for frustrated bosonic matter.
item.dc:creator: Yin-Kai Yu, Zhong-Chao Wei, Zi-Xiang Li

item.title: Boltzmann Equation and Hard Sphere Gas with Singular Initial Data: Well-posedness, Kinetic Limit, and Weak Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.31570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a local well-posedness theory for the spatially inhomogeneous 3-d Boltzmann equation with hard sphere cross-section, accommodating a class of large initial data. This class is an interpolation between the space $L_{x}^{\infty}L_v^{1}$ and $L_{v}^1L_{x}^{\infty}$ (with weight in $v$). It is notable for including data that can have infinite $L_{x,v}^\infty$-norm, entropy density. The core idea of the proof is a homogenization method based on collision geometries. As a key application, we prove the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with initial data in this space, having certain extra conditions. This is the first proof on the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with singular initial data. We also derive weak stability estimates of Boltzmann equation and hard sphere gas within the same functional spaces.
item.dc:creator: Chenjiayue Qi

item.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers. We apply it to two regimes: one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature, and finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding, Jianfeng Lu

item.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.31614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work constructs a non-trivial solution to the ill-defined two-dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation at criticality: a distribution-valued stochastic process on the plane, which we call the Critical 2D KPZ Process. It arises as the limit in law of centred log partition functions of two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers at criticality, viewed as discretised KPZ solutions. It is also a measurable function of the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) via a renormalised Cole-Hopf transformation, obtained as the limit of the centred logarithm of the spatially mollified SHF as the smoothing is removed. The Critical 2D KPZ process is non-Gaussian and its covariance displays a log-log blow-up near the diagonal. Gaussian fluctuations emerge when averaging on shrinking spatial scales. The results presented here were obtained through extensive interactions with generative AI (ChatGPT 5.5, 5.6 and 6); see Appendix C for more details. The proof builds on key recent and older advances in our field, combined in novel ways with substantial AI input. We view this manuscript as a "community project" that represents more than a decade's collective effort. We have worked on making the presentation as accessible as possible, highlighting the main ideas and their relations to the literature.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Berger, Francesco Caravenna, Jeremy Clark, Alexander Dunlap, Yu Gu, Ziyang Liu, Shuta Nakajima, Rongfeng Sun, Li-Cheng Tsai, Zuodi Xie, Nikos Zygouras

item.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's $L^2$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.31637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every $d\ge2$ and $0\le\sigma<1/3$, we construct with LLM-assistance a smooth bounded nonnegative lens-type potential $V$ with arbitrarily small $\|V\|_\infty+\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|x|^{1-d+\sigma}|V(x)|^2 dx$, such that $-\Delta+V$ has only pure point spectrum in $(0,\infty)$. Thus, we show that Barry Simon's $L^2$ conjecture, Problem 8 in "Schr\"odinger operators in the twenty-first century", is false.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Mengxuan Yang

item.title: On the direct SLE-martingale approach to the integrability of Conformal Loop Ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2610.31648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is about the derivation of "integrability results" (i.e., for example, explicit formulas for the probability of events involving a few marked points) for Conformal Loop Ensembles, that are the (conjectured) scaling limits of discrete crititical planar lattice models from Statistical Physics. We discuss the explicit solutions to the PDEs provided by the original SLE/CLE martingale approach that AI now makes it possible to uncover. This provides short and direct new proofs of a number of formulas that have recently been derived based on Liouville quantum gravity, conformal field theory or Coulomb gas methods, and also makes it possible to derive some new ones. We briefly illustrate this with the examples of the backbone exponent and annulus crossing probabilities for critical percolation, but this direct approach seems to apply to a wide class of observables of two-dimensional systems related to conformal field theories.
item.dc:creator: Jason Miller, Wendelin Werner

item.title: Ricci flow of Integrable Sigma Models, Hitchin Systems and Quantum Seiberg-Witten theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.31672v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a family of integrable 2d sigma models through 4d Chern-Simons theory and show that their classical point-particle reduction corresponds to a Hitchin system. The integrable Hitchin quantisation then provides a natural candidate Hamiltonian for the one-loop reduced dynamics of the sigma models, which coincides with the Perelman operator in all cases examined. This allows us to study the corresponding spectral problems using 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theory and 2d conformal field theory methods. For the sausage model, we derive exact quantisation conditions and compute exponentially small corrections essential for the agreement with numerical finite-volume results.
item.dc:creator: G. Bonelli, S. Lacroix, T. Pedroni, A. Tanzini

item.title: Recent Advances on a Model for the Electromagnetic Dirac Field at Thermal Equilibrium
item.description: arXiv:2609.11283v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We review recent progress on a model for the relativistic electron-positron field interacting with a classical electromagnetic field at positive temperature. The ultimate goal is to advance our comprehension of how thermal backgrounds affect polarisation mechanisms of this quantum system.
item.dc:creator: Umberto Morellini

item.title: Two-Species Boltzmann--Kac Kinetics with Matsumoto--Yor Nonlinear Collisions: Conserved Energy and Conic Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.18892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Mark Kac's kinetic framework from single-species Euclidean spaces to a two-species, non-linear interaction space on the open cone $(0, \infty)^2$ governed by the Matsumoto--Yor rational collision involution. We identify a non-linear conserved energy $E(x,y) = x + y + 1/x$ and an invariant conic metric measure $d\mu = \frac{dx \, dy}{x(x+y)}$. By establishing a two-species $H$-theorem, we prove that entropy production vanishes if and only if post-collision velocities are statistically independent ($I(U;V)=0$). In contrast to the transform-domain proof of Letac and Weso{\l}owski~\cite{letac2000}, which relies on joint Laplace transforms of general measures, our approach yields a direct physical derivation in state space via the transformation law for logarithmic gradients and separation of variables. This uncouples the functional-differential system to uniquely characterize the Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) and Gamma distributions as the non-equilibrium thermodynamic equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Itoh

item.title: Restricted variational principle for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2301.01721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the multifractal formalism for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles. We establish a variational relation between the Legendre transform of topological pressure of the generalized singular value function and measure-theoretic entropies. As a consequence, we show that the restricted variational principle of Lyapunov exponents holds for typical one-step cocycles. Furthermore, we prove a variational principle formula for the generalized singular value function.
item.dc:creator: Reza Mohammadpour

item.title: Operator quantum singular value transformation: Spectral mapping, design and topological invariants
item.description: arXiv:2401.09007v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) provides a unifying framework for quantum algorithms by applying the polynomials of quantum signal processing (QSP) to block-encoded matrices. We connect this framework with spectral analysis, design and topological protection in condensed matter physics. Extending QSVT beyond matrices to possibly infinite-dimensional operators (operator QSVT), we establish the following. First, it transforms every block of the operator by the QSP polynomials; no singular value decomposition is needed. Second, a spectral mapping theorem determines the full spectrum of the QSVT operator, including continuous spectra, from the embedded operator through the QSP polynomial, allowing spectral analysis without translation invariance. Third, the spectral mapping turns QSP into spectral design: the QSP phases can stretch, fold and separate the bands and place the eigenvalues. Finally, the kernel sectors that conventional QSVT usually sets aside carry a topological index, invariant under the choice of QSP phases, local perturbations and gap-preserving deformations, which guarantees topologically protected states. These results unify two quantum walks: Szegedy's walk from quantum algorithms and the split-step walk from condensed matter physics. Their kernel sectors encode the graph's Euler characteristic and the difference of bulk winding numbers, respectively. For the split-step walk, QSP breaks chiral symmetry but not the topological protection, and can move the protected state into a continuous band to form a bound state in the continuum (BIC).
item.dc:creator: Chusei Kiumi, Yohei Tanaka, Akito Suzuki

item.title: Sampling from Spherical Spin Glasses in Total Variation via Algorithmic Stochastic Localization
item.description: arXiv:2404.15651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of algorithmically sampling from the Gibbs measure of a mixed $p$-spin spherical spin glass. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that samples from the Gibbs measure up to vanishing total variation error, for any model whose mixture satisfies $$ \xi''(s) < \frac{1}{(1-s)^2}, \qquad \forall s\in [0,1). $$ Our algorithm follows the algorithmic stochastic localization (SL) approach introduced in (Alaoui, Montanari, Sellke, 2022) and in fact achieves a more difficult task. Namely, it (approximately) generates a sample path $({\boldsymbol y}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ from the SL process. For large $T$, ${\boldsymbol y}_T/T$ is an approximate sample from the target Gibbs measure, and hence we solve the original problem as a special case. We provide evidence that the condition $\xi''(s) < (1-s)^{-2}$ is sharp for the task of sampling SL sample paths. Furthermore, we prove that it is optimal within a class of generalized SL processes. Remarkably this threshold is close to the conjectured threshold for sampling from the original Gibbs measure. In particular, for the pure $p$-spin glasses it is within an absolute ($p$-independent) constant of the so-called shattering phase transition. Earlier work on related models was suboptimal by a factor diverging polynomially in $p$. A key step of this approach is to estimate the mean of a sequence of tilted measures. We produce an improved estimator for this task by identifying a suitable correction to the TAP fixed point selected by approximate message passing (AMP). As a consequence, we improve the algorithm's guarantee over previous work, from normalized Wasserstein to total variation error. In particular, the new algorithm and analysis open the way to perform inference about one-dimensional projections of the measure.
item.dc:creator: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: Exact WKB analysis of inverted triple-well: resonance, PT-symmetry breaking, and resurgence
item.description: arXiv:2604.05878v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study non-Hermitian quantum mechanics of an inverted triple-well potential within the exact WKB framework. For a single classical potential, different Siegert boundary conditions define three distinct quantum problems: the PT-symmetric, resonance, and anti-resonance systems. For each case, we derive the exact quantization condition and construct the associated trans-series solution. By identifying the resurgent structures and cancellations in these non-Hermitian setups, we obtain the median-summed series, clarifying when the spectra are real or complex in accordance with the physical properties of each system. Establishing explicit links to the semi-classical path integral formalism, we elucidate the roles of bounce and bion configurations in these non-Hermitian systems. This analysis predicts PT-symmetry breaking, which we also verify numerically. Using the median quantization conditions, we prove the existence of this symmetry breaking and establish an exact equation for the exceptional point, which emerges as a remarkably simple algebraic relation between the bounce and bion actions. We further show that the median-summed non-perturbative correction to the spectrum vanishes at the exceptional point, while the resurgent structure survives through a universal minimal trans-series. For the resonance and anti-resonance systems, we find that the exact median-summed spectra are related by complex conjugation, representing time reversal in this setting, are necessarily complex, and do not exhibit an exceptional point. Although their spectra differ significantly from the PT-symmetric case, they share the same minimal trans-series. By maintaining explicit links with the path integral saddles and the formal theory of resurgence, our analysis provides a unified and general perspective on the quantization of non-Hermitian theories.
item.dc:creator: Syo Kamata, Tatsuhiro Misumi, Cihan Pazarba\c{s}{\i}, Hidetoshi Taya

item.title: The Weyl-orbit embedding and a representation-theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2606.16862v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bu, Gu, and Jaffe introduced the quantum uniformity measures to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. We prove that the quantum uniformity measures are the pullbacks of the matrix-valued uniformity functionals of Gowers and Hatami under the map $U\mapsto(a\mapsto W_aUW_a^*)$, which we call the Weyl-orbit embedding. We study the structure of the Weyl-orbit embedding, and among other results, establish a canonical decomposition of the ambient matrix-valued uniformity space into uniformity preserving twisted copies of the quantum uniformity space. The Weyl-orbit embedding identifies the Clifford hierarchy with Leibman polynomial maps. This identification yields a representation theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy in terms of unitary representations of the universal polynomial groups introduced by the first author and Thom.
item.dc:creator: Asgar Jamneshan, Berke \"Unal

item.title: Integral representations of quantum R\'enyi divergences on von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.21214v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an integral representation of the $\alpha$-$z$ R\'enyi divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Along each ray $z=c\alpha$, the divergence is a positive average of relative entropies evaluated in a canonical family of escort states. For orders $\alpha$ above one, we require the divergence to be finite, whereas for orders below one support inclusion suffices. An explicit boundary correction removes the lower-order support assumption. The proof uses a compatible weighted Haagerup $L^p$ scale and applies outside the data-processing region. For faithful density matrices, we express the derivative of the escort relative entropy with respect to the R\'enyi order in terms of a nonnegative fluctuation quantity. Differences of order-one derivatives of the divergence give quantum Fisher information and Wigner-Yanase skew information. For faithful bipartite density matrices, we also express optimized conditional $\alpha$-$z$ entropies at orders above one as averages of ordinary conditional entropies. Further applications concern coherent-state divergences in quantum field theory and the optimizing order for the strong converse exponent in hypothesis-testing.
item.dc:creator: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy

item.title: Decoupling candidate dual AGN from chance superpositions in the GOTHIC survey via a deep-learning framework
item.description: arXiv:2608.24164v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dual active galactic nuclei (DAGN) mark a critical phase in the evolution of merging galaxies and the pairing of supermassive black holes, yet they remain difficult to identify in large imaging surveys because of projection effects and limited spatial resolution. Compact foreground stars and unresolved substructure can mimic dual nuclei through chance superposition, complicating automated detection. We revisit the 46,061 galaxies flagged but rejected as DAGN candidates by the GOTHIC pipeline, primarily because the two nuclei fell within the SDSS fibre aperture or exceeded its separation threshold. We train a supervised deep-learning framework based on the YOLOv11 oriented-bounding-box architecture on annotated SDSS imaging to separate genuine dual nuclei from foreground stellar contaminants and other spurious alignments. The final model attains a validation precision of 0.919, recall of 0.905, and $F_1$ of 0.912, and yields 29,605 dual-nucleus candidates after removing star-dominated and blended detections. Structured visual inspection indicates that $54.5$--$62\%$ are consistent with genuine dual nuclei, implying $\sim(1.4$--$1.8)\times10^{4}$ plausible systems. Cross-calibrating the YOLO separation against the deterministic GOTHIC centroid measurement and restricting to the compact regime ($d \le 6.87''$) gives a conservative subset of $\sim 13{,}672$ candidates, reaching calibrated separations of $\sim 0.56''$. Spectroscopy of the most compact ($\le 1$~kpc) systems shows spectra dominated by stellar absorption, with no resolved double-peaked emission, so confirmation requires higher-resolution follow-up. The catalogue is a statistically refined list of candidates, not confirmed DAGN. Nonetheless, deep-learning detection substantially reduces contamination and expands the plausible DAGN census.
item.dc:creator: Bhavesh Mukheja, Snehanshu Saha, Anwesh Bhattacharya, Mousumi Das, Fran\c{c}oise Combes, Sudhanshu Barway

item.title: Covariant Phase Space and Carroll-Weyl $\chi$ Symmetry of Carroll Non-BPS D$_p$-branes
item.description: arXiv:2609.08874v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze the covariant phase space of Kluso\v{n}'s canonical Carroll non-BPS D$_p$-brane actions. The Carroll limit is formulated as a contraction of the canonical phase space: the canonical one-form is invariant under the scaling of conjugate pairs, while the leading Hamiltonian constraint differs between the electric-like and magnetic-like sectors. This difference controls the weak closure of the electric-like constraint algebra and the stronger closure of the magnetic-like Hamiltonian brackets. We separate the generic non-BPS sector, which carries $D-1$ local phase-space degrees of freedom, from the tachyon-vacuum sector, which carries $D-2$ only after imposing second-class background conditions. We also identify the rank condition for the generic electric-like sector and its strengthening in the vacuum sector. Finally, we show that the Carroll--Weyl $\chi$ transformation, the matter-sector analogue of the null-string Carroll--Weyl symmetry, preserves the symplectic form and admits a charge, but is obstructed by the constraints and cannot be promoted to a first-class gauge generator except in highly restricted corners, a global vacuum sector or the singular potential $V\propto T^{-1}$ at $p=1$. The obstruction is algebraic in $\chi$, so no restriction of its spacetime profile can remove it. This contrasts with null string theory, where a restricted $\chi$-symmetry can be completed to an additional first-class constraint.
item.dc:creator: Limin Zeng

item.title: Moments Comparison Inequalities for Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow, Polymers and GMC
item.description: arXiv:2609.12820v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We employ a Gaussian convex inequality developed in [AC15], [Che26], [Gue22], and [FUMPC26] to establish (one sided) moment comparison inequalities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos, directed polymers in Gaussian environment and, in particular, the Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF), including upper bounds on negative moments, as well as similar lower bounds for $p$-th moments with $p\in (0,1)$. For the Critical 2d SHF, averaged over small balls, we also obtain the matching (up to multiplicative constants) complementary bounds. We establish the complementary bounds using a bootstrap argument inspired by [DS10] and a geometric decomposition introduced in [GT26]. Specifically, we prove that for locally averaged SHF, for every $p\in\mathbb R$, the $p$-th moment is, up to multiplicative constants, bounded in both sides by the $\frac{p(p-1)}{2}$-th power of its second moment.
item.dc:creator: Ziyang Liu, Zuodi Xie

item.title: Relaxation and Steady-State Entropy Production for Langevin SPDEs: A Dirichlet-Form Approach
item.description: arXiv:2609.18201v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Dirichlet-form framework for relaxation and steady-state entropy production in preconditioned Langevin stochastic partial differential equations. In infinite dimensions, the usual Fokker--Planck calculations based on ambient Lebesgue densities and the corresponding probability-current densities are generally unavailable. For the detailed-balance class, a quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet form on the Gibbs state space yields an exact de Bruijn entropy-dissipation formula for regular densities and an integrated inequality for arbitrary finite-entropy initial laws. Self-adjointness gives detailed balance and stationary path reversal, while a coordinate-martingale criterion identifies the associated process with the prescribed SPDE. For the one-dimensional $\Phi^4_1$ and convex Allen--Cahn-type Gibbs dynamics, we combine the established strong well-posedness theory with direct verification of the logarithmic derivatives, form closure, quasi-regularity and form--SPDE correspondence, and obtain relative-entropy decay bounds with exponents $2$ and $2(1-\lambda/m)$, respectively, with $m>\lambda$ in the latter case. Away from detailed balance, bounded skew-adjoint linear forcing preserves a Gaussian invariant law without requiring commutation between the forcing and covariance. We identify the antisymmetric action on cylinder observables and its Cameron--Martin current and prove that the squared current energy equals the steady-state entropy-production rate defined by forward--reverse path-space relative entropy per unit time, as well as the monotone limit of the Galerkin rates. Under commutation, we additionally obtain an explicit transient Onsager decomposition after a mass quench. Exclusion processes and Gaussian rotors provide finite-state and Gaussian benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Shuyuan Fan, Yuanke Chen, Lifei Wang, Jinqiao Duan

item.title: Gravitational Memory: an approximate description
item.description: arXiv:2609.39694v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Plane gravitational waves play a role both in relativistic and in non-relativisitic physics, highlighted by two different mass parameters. The large-distance behaviour of a sandwich gravitational wave can be approximated by a continuous but not necessarily smooth profile, providing us with a simplified description of particle motion. Our model is consistent with the Carroll symmetry. Our strategy is illustrated by the P\"oschl-Teller profile. The limitations of the sandwich approximation are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Q. -L. Zhao, P. -M. Zhang, M. Elbistan, J. Balog, P. A. Horvathy

item.title: Strong freezing in binary perceptron models
item.description: arXiv:2610.06275v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The binary perceptron model concerns the set of solutions obtained by intersecting random half-spaces. One of the most striking physics predictions for this model, going back to Krauth and M\'ezard [KM89] and sharpened in [HWK13, HK14], is strong freezing: typical solutions are at Hamming distance of order $n$ from every other solution. This phenomenon has attracted a lot of attention over the years, partly because of its intricate connections to statistical physics and computational complexity. We prove strong freezing at every positive constraint density for a general class of perceptron models and for any disorder with independent entries of mean zero and unit variance. More precisely, with probability at least $1-e^{-c\sqrt n}$, all but an $e^{-c\sqrt n}$ fraction of the solutions have no other solution within Hamming distance $\delta n$. In particular, our result includes the asymmetric binary perceptron at every margin, for which strong freezing has been a long-standing open problem [KM89,HWK13,HK14], and the symmetric binary perceptron, for which we recover the strong freezing results of Perkins and Xu [PX24] and of Abbe, Li and Sly [ALS21]. Our proof crucially relies on replacing the number of constraints by a Poisson variable, which makes the numbers of constraints cutting out different subsets of the hypercube independent. Since each constraint can only remove solutions, the FKG inequality then decouples the partition function from the event that two nearby configurations are both solutions.
item.dc:creator: Shuyang Gong, Shuangping Li

item.title: On wave operators for Hardy operators with and without perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2610.08594v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove asymptotic completeness of the wave operators in time-dependent scattering theory which intertwine the ordinary or fractional Laplacian and the corresponding Hardy operator, i.e., the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical or critical Hardy potential, whenever the Hardy potential is short-range. Moreover, we prove asymptotic completeness of the wave operators intertwining Hardy operators with and without external short-range perturbations. We also show the nonexistence of the considered wave operators when the Hardy or external potentials are long-range. We arrive at these results using three different approaches. The first approach uses an abstract semigroup framework for asymptotic completeness of wave operators for Fourier multipliers with short-range potentials. The second approach uses Kato smoothness theory. In the third approach, we develop and apply new propagation estimates for Hardy operators with and without perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Ishida, Konstantin Merz

item.title: Exponential decay of fractional moments in the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.10982v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$, we show that, at energy zero, the fractional moments of Green functions, $\mathbb E[ G(x,y)^s]$ decay exponentially in the distance between $x$ and $y$, for every constant edge weight $W>0$ and every $0<s<1/2$. Here $ G$ is the infinite-volume Green function of the associated random Schr\"odinger operator. The main ingredient is a quantitative lower bound on the derivative of the mean effective conductance with respect to the edge weights.
item.dc:creator: Jinglin Wang, Xiaolin Zeng

item.title: A mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy field
item.description: arXiv:2610.24865v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Foraging recruitment is a contagion: an agent that finds a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade, the model built for rumour and adoption spread on social networks, now embedded in space. Because activation is degree-normalized, the same rule that spreads the cascade also stifles it as neighbourhoods crowd, so the swarm aggregates on a resource and then releases to explore again. The cascade runs on the communication network, but acting on it moves agents in physical space, and that motion rewires the network: network and space are one coupled system, and this feedback, not any tuning, makes the coordination self-limiting. Because recruitment chains along the graph rather than reaching near neighbours alone, whether a discovery stays local or spans the swarm is a question of percolation. The swarm holds itself in a cascade window that is locally near-critical though globally subcritical, a self-organized, self-limiting drive-release cycle, sandpile-like but non-conservative. Nothing is tuned, yet behaviours that foraging biology documents separately emerge together: recruitment to discoveries, marginal-value patch-leaving, and Levy search with a switch to local exploitation. These follow from one least-committal principle, the resource field and the search both as maximum entropy, with Levy search matched to the field's sparsity and recruitment to its clustering, so active-matter order and optimal foraging appear as one system seen in two domains. The gains are real but conditional: up to 7.6x the harvest of solitary search when resources are sparse and clustered, shrinking to nothing when search is already easy. That sparse, clustered field is also the generic one, because resources almost inevitably aggregate, so one untuned rule should recur widely.
item.dc:creator: Galen J. Wilkerson

item.title: Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.27218v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.
item.dc:creator: Ihsan Topaloglu

item.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodictive tests: a unifying classical variational principle
item.description: arXiv:2610.29696v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The same classical f-divergence admits inequivalent extensions to quantum states. The question is whether these extensions can be obtained from a common classical variational principle with an operational interpretation. Here we generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by introducing retrodictive tests relative to a reference state. A retrodictive test compares a forward and a reverse stochastic process, realized by quantum preparation and measurement, related by Petz transposition relative to the chosen reference, and subject to prescribed quantum averages. Equivalently, it compares two reverse tests sharing a reference output, whose labels are coupled by retrodiction. For faithful states in finite dimension, we prove that the same spectral implementation attains the minimum classical f-divergence over all admissible implementations simultaneously for every operator-convex f. A flat reference yields the standard quantum f-divergences, thereby giving the Nussbaum-Szko{\l}a distributions a variational characterization. Choosing either prescribed state as reference recovers maximal quantum f-divergences and Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization, while power references interpolate between the standard and maximal divergences along the geodesic family. In the relative-entropy case, this gives the passage from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy by changing the reference state. The same optimization extends to arbitrary quantum channels and, for channels with faithful Choi operator, gives a variational characterization of quantum entropy production.
